newsitem.title: USA: US bill on China WTO entry to be introduced.
newsitem.headline: US bill on China WTO entry to be introduced.

text.p: House Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt plans to introduce a bill that would require a Congressional vote on U.S. approval of China's entry into the World Trade Organization, an aide said Tuesday.

It is the same bill the Missouri Democrat supported last year and some trade analysts believe it could gain broad support in light of recent allegations that China may have tried to funnel money into U.S. election campaigns.
The White House has argued that the legislation is not needed because of ongoing consultations with Congress on the the issue.

The bill requires a congressional vote prior to the United States giving its support to China's entry bid. A Gephardt aide said the congressman is looking to get good bipartisan support for the measure, which he said ensures that Congress is able to exercise its constitutional authority over international trade. Some analysts believe the China campaign contributions scandal could give some new support to the proposal.

"There are a lot of members on both sides of the aisle who have expressed interest in this issues before," said Greg Mastel trade analyst with the Economic Strategy Institute. He suggested the administration may be in no position to put up a fight.

"It's the kind of issue where because of the political sensitivities unique to the situation and because of the larger issue of Congress' involvement in trade, it might be hard for the administration to resist," he said.

Negotiations with China on its bid to join the Geneva-based trading body jumped forward in the latest round of talks in early March with a new offer by China to drop some of its trade barriers and bring some of its trading rules in line with the global body.
